title: Enterprise CPG Revenue Growth Management (RGM), Trade Promotion Optimization (TPO), Lift Decomposition & Deductions Agent

tiers.tier: Tier 1: Last-Year Roll-Forward Excel Calendar + Unaudited Retailer Chargeback Deductions
tiers.architecture: Copying last year's promotional calendar in Excel + counting raw promo-week shipment spikes as 'true lift' + auto-writing off <$10K retailer deductions

tiers.tier: Tier 2: Prompt-Only General LLM Promo Calendar Planner & Deduction Dispute Writer
tiers.architecture: Asking a general LLM to design BOGO/discount calendars and draft retailer dispute letters without elasticity or EDI 812 reconciliation

tiers.tier: Tier 3: Own-Price Elasticity Regression Only (Ignores Forward-Buy Dip & Cross-SKU Cannibalization)
tiers.architecture: Single-SKU log-log price regression on POS scan data without post-promo pantry-loading dip, sister-SKU cannibalization, or EDI 812/856 matching

tiers.tier: Tier 4: Hierarchical Cross-Elasticity + Pantry-Dip Decomposition + JBP Calendar MILP + EDI 812 Deduction Agent
tiers.architecture: Bayesian Hierarchical Own/Cross/Pantry-Dip Decomposition + Joint Business Plan (JBP) Guardrail MILP + Circular VLM + EDI 812/856/POS Deduction Clawback Agent

scenarios.scenario: Decomposing True Incremental Lift vs. Pantry-Loading Forward-Buy & Sister-SKU Cannibalization
scenarios.question: A 30%-off promotion on 24-pack Sparkling Water shows +140% promo-week shipment spike; evaluate whether to repeat the event
scenarios.model_answer: Decompose POS scan + shipment data: +140% gross spike consists of 52% retailer forward-buying, 38% consumer pantry-loading (4-week post-promo trough), and 34% cannibalization of higher-margin 12-pack SKU -> Net Incremental Margin ROI = -28% (cancel & replace with 15% multi-buy + endcap display)
scenarios.tier1_3_failure: Tier 1 & Tier 3 celebrate the +140% promo-week spike as 'pure incremental growth' and repeat a promotion that destroys $180K in net margin (58.4% negative-ROI promo share).

scenarios.scenario: Retailer Trade-Spend Deduction & Chargeback Audit (`EDI 812` vs. `POS Scan` + Circular Proof VLM)
scenarios.question: Retailer #4 deducts $164,000 off Invoice #9081 via EDI 812 claiming 82,000 units sold on a $2.00/unit scan-down allowance + feature-ad compliance
scenarios.model_answer: Reconcile EDI 812 debit memo against syndicated POS scan feed (actual promo scans = 58,400 units) and verify circular VLM proof-of-performance -> flag $47,200 unauthorized over-deduction and auto-submit dispute package to retailer portal (0.2% leakage)
scenarios.tier1_3_failure: Tier 1 finance team lacks line-item POS scan reconciliation and writes off the $47,200 over-deduction (11.6% deduction leakage).

scenarios.scenario: Joint Business Plan (JBP) 52-Week Promotional Calendar MILP (Price Floors & Conflict Rules)
scenarios.question: Optimize 52-week trade calendar across 6 national retail banners and 420 CPG SKUs under a $45M quarterly trade budget
scenarios.model_answer: Solve 52-week JBP MILP enforcing minimum 3-week recovery cool-down between deep discounts, brand-equity price floors, and non-overlapping hero-SKU promotions while synchronizing CPFR factory safety stock (0.9% promo OOS)
scenarios.tier1_3_failure: Tier 1 schedules simultaneous 35%-off promos across two retail banners without factory lead-time sync, causing a 14.2% on-shelf availability (OSA) stockout.

scenarios.scenario: In-Store Endcap Display & Feature Circular Compliance Computer Vision (`VLM` Audit)
scenarios.question: CPG brand pays $220,000 slotting/display fee for front-of-store endcaps across 1,400 stores during Holiday Week #48
scenarios.model_answer: Field-rep smartphone VLM verifies planogram facings, promotional price-tag placement, and endcap presence across store visits -> withhold/claw back display allowance on non-compliant stores
scenarios.tier1_3_failure: 35% of paid endcap displays are never erected in store, yet CPG brand pays 100% of fixed display allowances.

perturbation_checks.check: Competitor Counter-Promotion Shock (Rival Brand Drops Price -25% During Planned Event Week)
perturbation_checks.perturbed: 2.9% Net Margin MAPE | 3.8% Negative-ROI Share (Cross-Brand Competitive Price Index Term in Bayesian Hierarchy)

perturbation_checks.check: Brand-Equity Minimum Advertised Price (MAP) & Retailer Margin Floor Guardrail
perturbation_checks.perturbed: 0.0% Violation (Hard MILP Constraint Blocks Any Discount Below MAP Floor)

key_findings: Tier 4 (Bayesian Hierarchical Own/Cross/Pantry-Dip Lift Decomposition + 52-Week JBP Calendar MILP + EDI 812/POS Deduction Clawback Agent) slashes value-destroying negative-ROI promotions from 58.4% to 3.2% and net margin forecast MAPE from 29.5% to 2.4%.
Subtracting retailer forward-buying, consumer post-promo pantry-loading dips, and sister-SKU cannibalization reveals that over half of legacy 'high-volume' CPG promotions actually lose net margin.

Cross-checking retailer EDI 812 chargeback deductions against actual POS scan-down volumes and circular/endcap VLM proof-of-performance cuts invalid deduction leakage from 11.6% to 0.2%, reducing monthly trade-spend and deduction waste from $1.38M to $115K (-91.7%).
